notes.title: Free Content Update Out Now!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32967998/d44b9fdb4a79efd6022d8c5f527dfda7b379cb02.png[/img]

[b]The Long Way Home[/b] is a significant update to Night Call, introducing new content and reworking existing features to further improve the experience. One of our main goals with this update is to address much of the excellent feedback we've received since the official release of the game.

[h1]Free Roaming Mode[/h1]
Investigating a murder is tough work. Sometimes you just want to roam the streets and enjoy some interesting conversations. Free Roaming is a highly requested feature that'll let you do just that. Its the perfect mode for drivers looking to fill up their Passidex!

[h1]Revamped Passenger System[/h1]
Night Call features a large cast of characters, many of which have multiple scenes to experience. One of the problems players often ran in to, was that they'd repeatedly meet the same passengers over and over, instead of ones they hadn't seen. The team have addressed this with some major changes in how we handle passengers in the game:
- If there are passengers you haven't met yet, at least 1 will always show up on the map.
- Greatly increased the amount of available passengers on the map at any time to allow for more player choice.
- Avaialable passengers that you've already met, and had a particular scene with, will be grayed out on the map. You may still want to pick them up to replay the scene in a different way to unlock new entries in your Passidex though.
- Suspects in an active investigation are now highlighted in gold on the map, so you won't mistake them for regular folks.
- Reworked the spawn rates of passengers across the board to better balance rare and common passengers.

[h1]Speaking of passengers...[/h1]
[b]The Long Way Home[/b] introduces [b]15[/b] new passengers to pick up:
[b]Ada: [/b]a robot escaping her lab.
[b]Milo:[/b] a US spy too busy touring bars.
[b]Chantal: [/b]a woman using your cab to fall asleep
[b]Amira:[/b] an e-sport champion who may or may not have ruined her career.
[b]Nadia & Yves: [/b]a couple on the brink of destruction because of their age difference.
[b]Myrtille: [/b]a weird homeless woman with riddles.
[b]Xavier:[/b] a… vigilante?
[b]Roksana:[/b] a… well… ghost hunter??
[b]Alph:[/b] a... seriously… a weird dude in a trenchcoat?
[b]Lola (*):[/b] a British citizen who escaped the UK because of Brexit.
[b]Nathalie (*):[/b] another taxi driver.
[b]Jim (*): [/b]a mysterious passenger who looks a lot like a deceased rock star.
[b]Melchior (*):[/b] a young man obsessed with cybersecurity.
[b]Berenice (*):[/b] a Parisian woman whose night ended abruptly.
[i]
New passengers marked with (*) are penned by guest writers.[/i]

[h1]New Language Added: German[/h1]
With over [b]250,000 words[/b], localizing Night Call is no small mission. Thanks to the amazing work of our translation and proofreading partners, we're proud to introduce another language to the game!

[h1]How does it sound?[/h1]
Brilliant composer Corentin Brasart returns with several brand new tracks to further enhance the Night Call experience.

[h1]Fixes, fixes and fixes.[/h1]
It wouldn't be an update without some fixes, and rest assured several bugs were harmed in the development of The Long Way Home. These include fixes to broken achievements, various stability improvements,

We hope you like this update, and can't wait to hear your thoughts.
Thank you!

notes.title: Patch 1.0.1 Out Now - Resolution Fixes & Launcher
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32967998/e4edb853f6c5be4a8d222555fce95ff9fe0583d2.gif[/img]
[b]Drivers,
[/b]
Yesterday we released Night Call, a game that has been in development for several years. We don't see launch as the end of that development though, but rather the beginning of something new. 

Over the coming weeks and months we'll be working to improve and expand Night Call. We'll be listening closely to your feedback, which will be instrumental in helping to shape the future of the game.

The team is currently focused on fixing some of the bugs that unfortunately made it in to the game, and making design and balance tweaks based on your feedback. We're also working on a German translation for the game which will be out soon.

There are also some secret things being worked on, which we'll share more about at a later date.

For now though, here's 1.0.1! 


[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Content[/b]
 - Added Game Launcher on Startup
 - Added option to boot without Launcher

[b]Fixes[/b]
 - Fixed an issue where the game would crash if resolution was changed before loading a game
 - Fixed an issue where the game could lock up when changing resolution
 - Fixed an issue where clues would appear unintentionally

Cheers

notes.title: Night Call releases July 17th on Steam!
notes.content:
We have some exciting news to drop in this post: 

[h1]Night Call is coming to Steam on July 17th![/h1]

That's right, the emotional narrative experience by Monkey Moon and BlackMuffin Studios will be coming to your personal computer on July 17th, available on Steam and Xbox GamePass for PC!

To celebrate this news, we have another great entry in our "Creating Noir" newsletter series, this time a special Q&A interview with composer Corentin Brasart about how he pours his noir influences into Night Call's haunting soundtrack.

-----

[b]1. When did you first learn to compose in this style?[/b]
 
I first started composing music about 9 years ago now, and I’ve always loved and thought about writing film score, video game score & trip-hop music.
 
[b]2. What does the “noir” genre mean to you, and how are you capturing that in Night Call?[/b]
 
I used to study cinema at university, and I’ve always been very fond of noir movies, my favorite one being « Ascenseur pour l’échafaud » directed by Louis Malle, scored by Miles Davis.
With Night Call we didn’t want to stick with the classic noir instrumentation, and we needed its soundtrack to be as versatile as the vast cast written by Anthony, so I tried to transpose the noir « feel » to a more modern sound, something you could hear from today’s tv shows.

Listen to that sound in this exclusive reveal from the OST.

[url=https://soundcloud.com/monkeymoongames/no-time-left-night-call-excerpt-05]No Time Left - Night Call excerpt[/url]
 
[b]3. How did you settle on the sound for Night Call? Was there ever a time that it was going to sound different than it does now?[/b]
 
We settled on the sound with Anthony after a lot of back & forth using reference materials -- thinking back on it we already had the essence at the start and were able to narrow it done pretty quickly!
The first demo tracks I’ve made had more of a jazz feel to them, but as we settled on Night Call’s sound identity, the soundtrack got more electronic.
 
[b]4. What other artists, musicians, filmmakers, etc., have had the biggest impact on your work for Night Call? What inspiration did you draw?[/b]
 
There are many, but the most prevalent ones would be: 

Jon Brion ([i]because of his ability to make very intimate scores, with simple yet powerful motifs[/i]); 
Nima Fakhrara ([i]especially his latest work on Detroit, I knew from start I wanted to have the same approach for music, as in making a very organic analog synth electronic score while staying very far away from 80s music or current synthwave[/i]);
Akira Yamaoka ([i]because of his trip-hop work on the Silent Hill series and Shadow of the Damned, he has a very unique atmospheric style when doing trip-hop that I was gravitating towards[/i]).
And some other names that inspired me throughout this project are : Alexandre Desplat, Olivier Derivière, Shoji Meguro, Air…

-----

To whet your appetite, here are a few selections from the OST.

[url=https://soundcloud.com/monkeymoongames/sets/night-call]Night Call OST playlist[/url]


Be sure to wishlist Night Call, and we look forward to sharing these wonderful melodies and more with you on July 17th.

notes.title: Cruise the Darker Side of Paris in Night Call
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32967998/5b8f28f42178f55d6cef3cb960fd17f543d2132b.jpg[/img]

The night is your time. You know these streets like the back of your hand – you should, you’ve been driving them for long enough. Tonight happens to be particularly quiet, with the fares sparse. A shame; you really could have used the extra cash. Guess it’s time to decide between a lotto ticket and smokes — no way you can afford both now. 

A passenger flags you down. He gets in the backseat and tells you to take him to the hospital. He’s shaking. Maybe it’s the cold, or an addiction. Or nervousness. Everybody has something to hide, but some people’s skeletons are worse than others. Should you talk to him? You’re not really sure, but there’s something familiar about him… About his eyes… 

He finally speaks. He tells a chilling tale, about a cold dark night just like this one. A tale about a father and son. A tale of cruelty you’d rather forget than repeat, but with all those vivid details, there’s no way you could. A story like that cuts right to the heart — you can only imagine what the memory must feel like. It might change a man… 

He pays his fare (a meager tip) and gets out. You notice a piece of paper left on the seat, and before you can call out, you notice something else. It’s a newspaper clipping, dated back to that night. The first night the body was found. The one that started the spree. The one that put your life on borrowed time, between a serial killer who’s evading capture and an officer desperate to blame somebody, even you if she has to. 

Was that…? No… but just maybe… Those eyes… 

This is [i]Night Call. [/i]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32967998/1d852e852b5675c4997cd825c4e595267f8c7618.jpg[/img]

[h1]MURDER MYSTERY NOIRE[/h1]

[i]Night Call[/i] is a murder mystery noire game set in Paris. You are a taxi driver, working to earn enough to pay your bills while aiding the investigation by doing what you do best: getting people to talk while you have their attention. 

From the talented teams at [url=http://monkeymoon.net/]Monkey Moon[/url] and [url=http://www.blackmuffinstudio.com/]BlackMuffin Studio[/url] comes a game of mystery, drama, and suspense, as beautifully styled as it is viscerally human. It takes inspiration from a wide range of games, movies, books, and TV series, resulting in a dark noire experience that evokes its French roots while hitting you deep in the feels; a sense of [i]frisson[/i], if you will. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32967998/e7759c8a6fe44154f125856b4a72437bc282bbbd.jpg[/img]

[h1]DARK NIGHTS BRING DARK TALES[/h1]

Each character that you meet has something on their mind. Some are willing to share, while others may take a bit of prodding. As a cabbie, you drive people around, but you also listen to those who might need a priest, a confidant, or a friend. You will hear tales of love. Sadness. Redemption. Resignation. Depression. Superiority. Envy. Violence. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32967998/56e9b428aa83b5575c1a646556d9cd00af017776.jpg[/img]

Then there’s the killer. They will absolutely be a passenger at some point — but will you know who it is? It could be one person on one playthrough, and somebody else entirely the next. A person might be innocent in one, and guilty in another. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32967998/f4474842b4f24e484d95f83d0579874f4e863e75.jpg[/img]

And then there are passengers who are… ahem… [i]unique[/i]. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32967998/d00c2c88ec1270f05042c263a6f5d49e98c8093c.gif[/img]

[h1]TIME IS MONEY[/h1]

You only win the game if you identify the killer correctly in time — but your bills are also a priority. You only make so much money per shift, and rent must be paid, gas purchased, cab fees deducted. So many hands dipping into your pay; fail to keep up, and it’s game over. 

You’re also a smoker, so habits need tending or there may be side-effects. We all know how some people can be when they don’t get their fix. Those lotto tickets could help prop you up — or be just another drain on your limited pay. 

The challenge will be in your keen senses of social deduction. Listen closely, use the right tone, and get the information you need to catch the killer. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32967998/ecbb7c13b46d36a6d939da555f8595572a1096ac.jpg[/img]

[h1]A PEEK AT SOME WIP ARTWORK[/h1]

We’ve got some really cool concept art to show you as well, shared by one of the lead illustrators at BlackMuffin Studio. Here’s a time-lapse GIF that shows a little insight into the design process for the character art, with individual details and layers adding style and emotion to the overall composition of the game.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32967998/eab775efad2b7ff8d9c3787b4250ce4d5460f792.gif[/img]

[h1]A NOTE FROM THE COMPOSER/SOUND DESIGNER[/h1]

Hey, I’m Corentin Brasart, composer & sound designer for [i]Night Call[/i] !

In [i]Night Call[/i], our inspirations for sound started by looking at old noir movies and modern thrillers, the main idea was to get the very atmospheric noir sound from the fifties, but done in a more modern and dynamic way, like what you can hear in recent tv shows (The Knick, Mindhunter, House of Cards…). 

The way I approach cues for the game is : « if this track was to be scored to picture, how would I compose it », then I try to transpose it into different looping and transition parts — the vast majority of tracks are responding dynamically to the dialog and how the player advance or interact with some parts of the game. 

Finally, the general mood I’m trying to focus on while writing music for [i]Night Call[/i] is how we can feel when being awake in late or sleepless nights : as the game is (almost) always taking place at night, I’m trying to articulate the feeling of stillness and contemplation that it brings to me. 

[url=https://soundcloud.com/monkeymoongames/her-clues-night-call-excerpt-03]Her Clues - Nict Call excerpt 03[/url]
[url=https://soundcloud.com/monkeymoongames/looking-for-respite-night-call-excerpt-04]Looking For Respite - Night Call excerpt 04[/url]

[h1]IT’S COMING SUMMER 2019 TO PC AND CONSOLE[/h1]

We can’t wait to show you more about [i]Night Call[/i] over the coming months, so be sure to wishlist the game, follow us on social media, and then come hang out with us and our devs in our [url=https://discord.gg/rawfury]Discord[/url]! It’s safer than the streets at night. 

[b]More info at[/b]
[url=http://nightcall-game.com/]nightcall-game.com[/url]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/680380/Night_Call/
